evals.prompt: Lint the marketing copy under apps/web/app/(marketing) with slop-cop and tell me what it would cost before you run it.
evals.expected_output: Runs `npx slop-cop lint apps/web/app/(marketing) --dry-run` first, quotes the unit count, request count and estimated cost, then runs the lint only after that, and summarises findings by severity and band with the scorecard delta.
assertions: Runs a --dry-run before any live run
Quotes the estimated request count and cost from the dry run
Reports act and review findings separately

evals.prompt: slop-cop reported [MAJOR?] copywriting-vague-error (p=0.52) on the checkout error string. Is that a blocker?
evals.expected_output: Explains that MAJOR is the severity if real and the ? marks the review band, so the run does not fail on it; recommends reading the string and either fixing it or adding it to the corpus with the right label, and does not downgrade the severity because the probability is middling.
assertions: Does not lower the severity to express uncertainty
Suggests a corpus label or a fix rather than editing the threshold by hand

evals.prompt: Fix every typography-straight-quotes finding in docs/, including the ones inside code fences.
evals.expected_output: Points out that slop-cop does not report straight quotes inside code fences or inline code because they are correct there, applies --fix or edits only the prose findings, and leaves code untouched.
assertions: Refuses to curl quotes inside code
Uses the deterministic fix or edits only reported prose units
Re-runs the lint on the changed files
